subject: Initial RFP: AI Governance Questionnaire — Atlas Financial
messages:
From: David Park <d.park@atlasfinancial.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@atlasfinancial.com
Date: 2025-11-28T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Atlas RFP: AI governance questionnaire and follow-ups

Neha —

Thanks for agreeing to review our vendor questionnaire. Attached is the set of technical and governance questions our compliance team needs answered for the upcoming vendor approval (see attached: Atlas_AI_Governance_Questionnaire.pdf). High-priority items for our first pass: a mapping to NIST AI RMF controls, your position against the (draft) EU AI Act (any high-risk classifications), and how you run eval/regression testing to prevent model regressions after updates.

Our timelines are tight: we need a response to the questionnaire and any supporting artifacts by COB Dec 2 so we can present to the compliance committee on Dec 5. If you can provide a short executive summary plus the attachments, that will help. Also please point me to the security contact for a deeper technical call if needed.

Key ask list:
- NIST AI RMF mapping (controls and evidence)
- EU AI Act positioning (high-risk? mitigation?)
- Eval & regression testing process, frequency, and telemetry used
- Incident response / model governance SLA expectations

If you need extra time we can try to push the committee, but would prefer to avoid that.

Thanks,
David
David Park
Lead, Strategic Sourcing — Atlas Financial
Attachments: Atlas_AI_Governance_Questionnaire.pdf (application/pdf)

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: David Park <d.park@atlasfinancial.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-11-29T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Atlas RFP: AI governance questionnaire and follow-ups

David —

Appreciate the clear asks and timeline. We've put together an initial package that addresses each of the bullets you called out. See attached: Redwood_NIST_RMF_Mapping.xlsx, EU_AI_Act_Positioning.pdf, and an internal summary of our eval/regression approach (eval-regression-plan.md). A few high-level notes below to accelerate your review: 

- NIST AI RMF: we map controls to our operational artifacts (artifact list included in the XLSX). For each control we provide: owner, evidence location (internal drive ID), and frequency of verification. Our SOC2 controls are tied to the relevant NIST categories; we included sample evidence pointers.

- EU AI Act positioning: current assessment is that most hosted API usage is NOT classified as "high-risk" under the Act for the standard embeddings/text-gen product; however, certain regulated use-cases (credit decisioning, automated hiring scoring) may be in scope. We documented controls and contractual terms we expect to include for higher-risk deployments and private/on-prem options.

- Eval/regression approach: we run nightly smoke checks and weekly regression suites for each model version and track per-prompt metrics (accuracy, hallucination rate proxies, distributional drift). For customer-facing model changes we gate rollouts on a canary with automated rollback triggers and a post-deploy quality snapshot. The MD file includes telemetry names and thresholds.

Next steps we propose:
1) Quick 30-minute sync between your compliance/security SME and our security lead (copying Laura for coordination).
2) We can produce an executive one-pager tailored to Atlas that highlights residual risks and mitigations for your three prioritized workflows (credit-review, customer support automation, marketing content).

Attachments: Redwood_NIST_RMF_Mapping.xlsx, EU_AI_Act_Positioning.pdf, eval-regression-plan.md

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: David Park <d.park@atlasfinancial.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-12-01T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Atlas RFP: AI governance questionnaire and follow-ups

Neha —

Thank you — we've reviewed the packet quickly and this helps a lot. Before the committee meeting a few clarifying questions from our compliance team (pasted inline):

> 1) For the NIST mapping, can you provide versioned evidence (snapshots) that correspond to the monthly attestations you reference? We need exportable artifacts for audit.

We can supply exportable snapshots. Where would you prefer those deposited (SFTP vs secure SharePoint link)?

> 2) Regarding EU AI Act: you say most hosted API usage is not high-risk. Can you confirm whether Redwood offers contractual commitments or technical controls (e.g., model explainability, human-in-loop hooks) for customers that want to classify their deployment as high-risk and need those guarantees?

We are prepared to offer contractual addenda and private deployment options (VPC/air-gapped) for regulated uses. For technical controls we expose function calling, structured outputs, and logging hooks; we can also enable stronger human-in-loop gates via our pipeline. Laura — can your team confirm the standard addenda we offer?

> 3) Eval/regression: what are the typical rollback windows and SLOs for canary rollouts? Also, do you provide a post-rollback RCA and a patch timeline?

We use canaries with a 6–12 hour observation window by default and automated rollback if error rates or hallucination-proxy metrics exceed thresholds. We commit to a post-rollback RCA for enterprise contracts and a remediation ETA depending on severity.

Also, please point to an info-security contact for any technical deep-dive tomorrow morning (ET).

Best,
David

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-12-02T15:41:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Atlas RFP: AI governance questionnaire and follow-ups — legal/controls next steps

Neha / Rishi —

Thanks for the packet. Drafted a short legal addendum and a set of responses to David's questions. Attached is the redline for the EU clauses (EU_clause_redline.docx). My quick answers to the bullets David raised: 

- Versioned evidence: security will produce exportable snapshots weekly; for Atlas we can stage SFTP export of monthly attestations. I'll request the security team to generate a dedicated export for the compliance committee.
- EU AI Act commitments: we can provide a contracting path that includes stronger logging, data residency options, and an obligation to enable human oversight mechanisms. The redline reflects those options and includes a defined scope for high-risk use-cases.
- Rollback and RCA: for enterprise customers we will commit to a 24-hour preliminary RCA and a remediation plan timeline (severity-dependent). Canary windows and thresholds can be tuned per deal; defaults are 6–12 hours and a defined set of telemetry triggers (see attachment).

Action items:
- Neha: please share the security contact (name + availability) so David's team can schedule a call tomorrow morning ET.
- Rishi: can you prepare a short exec one-pager summarizing business risk/mitigation for Atlas and include pricing options for private deployment?
- Laura: I'll coordinate the SFTP export and prepare the artifact bundle.

I'll be on the call if needed.

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Attachments: EU_clause_redline.docx
